cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pass Me the Authority
cards.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders the outgoing decision maker to name A; A3 dismisses possession of the chair and A5 approves the content but corrects its audience, preserving status throughout transfer pursuit.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 chair possession prompts A3 location/succession distinction; B4 private you are chairing prompts A5 public direction. Spoken address to A makes the audience correction intelligible though room acoustics are unstated.

relationship.evidence: B2 regards physical succession as sufficient and B4 gives the requested title reluctantly; A refuses to release B from public procedure.

heightening.evidence: B4 concedes the substance, causing A5 to demand its public delivery rather than invent another title.

specificity.evidence: A1 meeting and leaving role establish a handover; B2 chair is physical while B4 chairing is decision responsibility.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 I already agree makes A own endorsement comically irrelevant to the required transfer, earned by B4 direct address.
